Before the towering walls of a great besieged castle, siege-towers grinding forward, ladders clattering against scorched ramparts, the vast field below churned to ruin, smoke columns rising against a copper-stained sky.

A vast open plain stretching to a hazy horizon under a brooding storm-sky, two armies' lines running for miles in either direction, trampled grass and churned mud beneath an oppressive silence before the charge.

A narrow mountain pass choked wall-to-wall with struggling fighters, sheer cliff faces rising on both sides, the press of armored bodies receding into shadow and choking dust toward a distant sliver of grey sky.

The burning streets of a sacked city, fires roaring from every window, smoke blackening the sky above crumbling rooftops, the battle fragmenting into a thousand desperate struggles across rubble-strewn avenues stretching to the distant citadel.

A muddy river-crossing at low ford, men and horses floundering in brown churning water, the far bank bristling with defenders, the long bridge downstream already choked with struggling masses beneath a grey and weeping sky.

A snow-covered field of war, the white expanse stained crimson in vast arcs, frozen breath rising from thousands of fighters, dark banners stark against the pale sky, the treeline a black fringe at the far horizon.

The breached gate of a great fortress, the shattered portcullis hanging crooked, attackers pouring through the smoking gap, defenders pressing back from every parapet and courtyard wall, the battle raging deep into the keep beyond.

A long hilltop and its broad slopes, the defenders massed on the crest beneath a grey sky, the attackers surging upward across churned ground, the lowland battlefield spreading far and wide below in both directions.

An ash-strewn volcanic plain, grey cinders underfoot and black lava ridges splitting the field, sulphurous haze drifting low across the armies, distant cone-peaks smouldering against a bruised amber sky of terrible scale and desolation.

A misty moor stretching endlessly under a pale and featureless sky, the armies half-swallowed in rolling grey fog, dark shapes pressing forward through heather and bog, the battle muffled and vast and ghostly in all directions.
The great courtyard of a vast keep, high walls looming on every side, the space filled from gate to hall with the heave of battle, fire and smoke rising against a narrow slot of stormy sky above.

A desert battlefield of dust and dunes, sand-walls shifting in a scorching wind, the armies' lines broken and swallowed by rolling curtains of ochre dust, the sun a white disc above an ocean of battle.

A dense ancient forest where the armies have torn clearings with their passage, shafts of pale light cutting through the canopy, the battle spreading through shadowed corridors of oak and pine to a murky horizon of dark trunks.

A wide coastal beach at low tide, dark cliffs flanking both ends, the armies clashing across wet sand and rock pools, warships burning offshore and landing boats grinding aground through surf beneath a pale and windswept sky.

A frozen lake mid-winter, the ice cracked and groaning underfoot, men slipping and falling in vast struggling masses, dark water gleaming through fractures, the far shore a low dark line under a colourless enormous sky.

A ruined colosseum of enormous scale, shattered tiers rising on all sides, the arena floor a battleground of broken stone and sand, the fighting spilling up stairways and through archways under an open dome of grey sky.

A swampy delta where the armies wade through knee-deep black water, cypress roots and reed-beds breaking every formation, fires burning on dry hummocks, the whole vast wetland alive with desperate struggle under a low and murky sky.

A long stone bridge over a deep gorge, the narrow span packed solid with fighters, the chasm dropping away on both sides into shadow, the battle continuing onto both banks stretching wide in either direction.

Terraced farmland on a hillside, stone walls dividing tier after tier of trampled fields, the armies flowing up and down the steps of the landscape, smoke rising from burning farmsteads against a grey and overcast horizon.

A cliff-top fortress on a sea-headland, the walls battered by both siege-engines and crashing waves, the landward approach a chaos of camps and entrenchments stretching inland, the sea glittering cold and indifferent beyond the burning towers.

A subterranean cavern of colossal scale, stalactites hanging over a vast underground battlefield lit by fires and torches, the armies dwarfed by cathedral-high stone ceilings, the echoing roar of battle swallowed in the immense dark.

A wide valley between two long ridgelines, both heights held and fought over, the valley floor a churned no-man's-land of struggling formations, the whole scene framed by grey peaks receding to a distant and cloud-wrapped horizon.

Before a great harbour seawall, the battle raging across the dock-front and jetties, warships grappled alongside the quays, fire spreading from warehouse to warehouse along the waterfront, the harbour itself choked with struggling vessels and dark smoke.

A wind-blasted steppe under a vast and featureless sky, the two cavalry hosts spread in enormous sweeping lines across the flat and yellowed grass, dust plumes rising miles behind each wing as the charge reaches full thunder.

A deep ravine-cut badlands, red rock walls channelling the battle into a labyrinth of narrow defiles and sudden open spaces, the sky a jagged strip of pale blue above, the scale of the stone landscape dwarfing all armies.
